source_tamil_lines: கண்ணடிச்சு யாரை நீயும் கண்ணி வைக்கப் பார்க்குறே
என்னைக் கண்டு ஆசை கொண்டு ஏனோ சும்மா ஏங்குறே
ஏனோ சும்மா ஏங்குறே எண்ணி எண்ணி வீங்குறே (கண்)
english_lines: Who are you winking at, trying to set a snare?
Trying to set a snare—are you trying to fool me? (கண்)
Seeing me and desiring me, why do you just pine?
Why do you just pine, swelling as you think and think? (கண்)
notes: The colloquial teasing register is preserved rather than formalized.

english_lines: Take that face of yours and look at it in a mirror!
notes: The mocking compounds are kept deliberately blunt.

source_tamil_lines: கொல்லைக்காட்டு நரியைப் போலே பல்லைப் பல்லைக் காட்டுறே
நொள்ளைக் கண்ணும் யானைக்காதும் காண ரொம்ப ஜோரையா
english_lines: Like a fox from the fields, you bare tooth against tooth,
There is none to equal you, O odd-mouthed warrior!
Your squinting eye and elephant ears—what a grand sight, sir!
What a grand sight indeed—look in the mirror, sir!
notes: The verified source form `இருச்சவாய்` is difficult; `odd-mouthed` is a conservative rendering within the surrounding mock-beauty catalogue, without changing the Tamil.

english_lines: Crab-legged gait, O beauty; desert-land head, O beauty!
notes: `பாலைவனைத்` is a verified unusual source form; the English preserves its desert-land image instead of substituting a guessed familiar insult.

english_lines: Tall and lean in form like a camel,
Are two eyes enough just to behold your beauty? (என்)

translator_notes: This is a comic mock-beauty performance. Source insults and animal/body imagery are retained rather than softened.
Item-level lyric authorship remains unresolved at this booklet-evidence tier; translation does not upgrade attribution.
